grade.first_issue: None; the proof is complete and correct by normal Olympiad standards.
grade.summary: The submission correctly proves that Mulan can guarantee victory exactly when θ=180°/n for an integer n≥2. The sufficiency argument forces both children into the set of positive multiples of θ, and the necessity argument gives Shan-Yu an invariant strategy preserving triangles with no such angle.
strengths: Correctly parametrizes all admissible cuts and the angles of both child triangles.
Proves by induction that any triangle containing a positive multiple of θ is winning.
For θ=180°/n, correctly finds an admissible multiple of θ in the relevant interval so both children are winning.
For all other θ, exhausts the four ways both children could contain multiples of θ and derives a contradiction in each case.
Correctly uses the resulting invariant to give Shan-Yu a perpetual avoidance strategy from a suitable initial triangle.
